questions.question: How much of RFC-0021 Appendix A should the kernel implement in #1127?

options.label: All but links (Recommended)
options.description: A.1–A.6, A.8–A.10 in the kernel and spec 003: unconditional A.4 write checks (kernel drops reject_write_under_file_ancestor), A.3 omission + byte-order obligation + flat folder-op stat, A.8 tables for every call. A.7 links land with the first link driver (Local/SFTP), spec 003 marks them [~]. Fake gains item+prefix-on-one-page.

options.label: All of Appendix A
options.description: Also add the `links` driver declaration, follow_within_root/no_follow policy and A.7's entry rules to the kernel now, tested on the fake only. Largest PR; links logic has no real driver until Local/SFTP move.

options.label: Handoff list only
options.description: Spec 003 section, delete_folder + classifier from A.8, 7 threads, A.10 suites. A.3/A.4 behaviour changes deferred to BK-394; spec 003 marks them [~] and A.10's encoding suite covers only A.8. Smaller, but spec and kernel disagree until BK-394.

options.label: New backlog item (Recommended)
options.description: File a BK item ("glob on the kernel skips A.3 on a flat namespace") with the stated gap as its body; BE-032 cites it. Repo stays honest per principle 3, work lands with the first flat driver.

options.label: Implement in #1127
options.description: Add the literal-prefix stat now and a set-based omission over glob matches (no byte order to rely on). More kernel surface for the closing round to review.

options.label: Leave as stated
options.description: Keep the sentence in BE-032 with no item; a later migration finds it.
